## Counts (endorsed rows)
- Headline claims: 18.
- Joint claims: 2 (C7, C10). Clashes: 0.
- Claims in at least one endorsed relation: 10 (56%); 7 relations, all covers.

## Joint claims
- C7 (barriers): interview themes (F14-F17, Q) + survey variation by focus and low domain scores (F2, F7, F8, N), argued as "consistent with" at p.68; confirm.
- C10 (structured activities to raise shared knowledge and mutual respect): domain scores (F6, F7, N, Discussion p.69) + cloud-meeting theme (F10, Q, p.64, p.70); expand.

## Points to check
1. C7: rule 7 joins only the self-interest element of the barrier list to the survey; limiting rests_on to F14-F17 gives 1 joint claim.
2. C10: F6 shows mutual respect is already the highest domain, so the survey supports the shared-knowledge half only; the Discussion argument is framed conditionally ("may offer opportunity").
3. C2 and C3 overstate the tests (curative vs all others; population and preventive not different); record as a reporting inconsistency.
4. R7 (C10 covers C17) is the weakest relation: the abstract does not name the cloud meetings. Rejecting it gives 9 claims related (50%), as C10 is in no other relation.
5. C8: the Discussion's second "novel theme" (p.70) rests on the rule-12 comparison (F21); if A1 counts it as one of the "emergent factors", C8 becomes joint (3).
